newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint eases vs basket on Czech, Polish problems.
newsitem.headline: Forint eases vs basket on Czech, Polish problems.

text.p: The forint opened weaker against a bullish dollar and eased versus its currency basket as Polish and Czech floods and trade balance uncertainties mixed some volatility into Hungarian trading too, dealers said.

"Some investors have got scared that the central European events could touch Hungary as well," said Pal Szucs of Hypo-Bank Hungaria, adding that the fears would be temporary. "Some uncertainty is felt, but not panic."
The forint opened at 193.22/27 and stood at 193.35/40 at 0813 GMT, well below Monday's closing.

The Hungarian unit, which usually trades at the National Bank of Hungary's resistance level (NBH bid), moved some eight fillers below the NBH bid at the opening but later reduced the gap to five fillers.

Recent floods to the north of Hungary, foreigners' concerns over the Czech and Polish trade deficits and an ailing zloty increased the probability for the forint of a 30 filler drop within the NBH intervention band, dealers said.

Influenced by the Czech and Polish events and a recent Deutsche Morgan Grenfell report saying that trade balance problems may return in Hungary as well, some investors withdrew funds from the Hungarian market too, mainly from government securities, Szucs said.

However, most macro-eceonomic news was positive and more capital flowed into the country than out, dealers said, adding that the forint was likely to return to the NBH bid as it has in the past eighteen months.
